title: The 1919 eclipse measured a deflection of starlight
summary: Dyson, Eddington, and Davidson reported a solar deflection of light from the 29 May 1919 eclipse.
body: Frank Watson Dyson, Arthur Stanley Eddington, and C. Davidson published observations from the total solar eclipse of 29 May 1919. Their paper reports a deflection of starlight by the Sun's gravitational field. It is one early observational test associated with general relativity. Later work has re-examined the plates and the error bars; the 1920 paper remains the primary report of that expedition, not the last word on measurement precision.
